title: Recovering an Orchard’s Pollinators
transcript: An orchard may have plenty of blossom and still attract surprisingly few insects. The study I want to describe began with a row of apple trees beside a disused railway. Along the fence, the researchers sowed clover, which flowers before the apple trees and gives insects an early food source. During the trial, cameras recorded visits to selected branches every afternoon. A matching row at the opposite edge of the orchard had only grass beneath it and provided a comparison. The clover row attracted more small wild bees, even on the coolest days, but the number of honeybees hardly changed. This difference mattered because the orchard already had several managed hives nearby. The researchers now plan to follow the same rows for another season. Their first trial measured visits to flowers, so it could not tell them whether more apples were produced.

questions.prompt: The first row of trees was beside a disused ____.
questions.explanation: 研究人员首先选中了废弃铁路旁的一排苹果树。

questions.prompt: The researchers planted ____ to provide an early food source.
questions.explanation: 三叶草比苹果树开花早，能提前为昆虫提供食物。

questions.prompt: Visits to the branches were recorded using ____.
questions.explanation: 研究人员每天下午使用摄像机记录昆虫访花。

questions.prompt: Which group showed a clear increase in visits?
questions.explanation: 种了三叶草的一排树吸引了更多小型野生蜂，蜜蜂数量则几乎未变。

questions.prompt: What could the first trial not determine?
options: Whether insects visited on cooler days
Whether there were managed hives nearby
Whether the trees yielded more fruit
questions.answer: Whether the trees yielded more fruit
questions.explanation: 首次试验只测访花次数，未能判断苹果产量是否增加。
